brief: We know little of the life of Julian beyond the fact that she was born about 1342, became a recluse and lived in a cell attached to the Church of St Julian in Conisford, Norwich, and died sometime after 1416. She is best known for her book, The Revelations of Divine Love, one of the finest of English mystical writings. It reveals the depth of her spiritual awareness. Her strong convictions in the victory of God’s love led to her famous saying, “Sin is inevitable, but all shall be well, and all shall be well, and all manner of things shall be well.”
